misses.answer: No. Including an AsyncInferenceConfig object in the endpoint configuration means the endpoint can receive asynchronous invocations. It cannot also serve synchronous real-time requests. Asynchronous endpoints are invoked with InvokeEndpointAsync, with the request payload placed in Amazon S3. If you need both modes, you would need to deploy separate endpoints: one asynchronous and one real-time (without AsyncInferenceConfig).

misses.answer: No, you can't switch the type. The workflow type can't be updated after you create a state machine, so an Express workflow stays Express. To get 90 days of history, either (1) create a new Standard state machine with the same definition and role and point callers at it, since Standard workflows let you retrieve full execution history via the Step Functions API for up to 90 days after an execution completes; or (2) keep the Express workflow, enable logging to CloudWatch Logs, and set the log group's retention to at least 90 days, because log data is kept indefinitely but can be configured. I did not confirm the exact Express history retention behavior or the logging setup steps in the docs, so verify those before relying on option 2.
